messages:
maria.chen: Heads-up — product asked us to finalize the audit event naming and customer-visible examples this week. They want clear guidance for RBAC changes + KMS interactions before the next release.

daniel.k: thanks — can you paste the current event sample we ship to customers? want to see what needs changing.

maria.chen: current example (internal):\n```json\n{\n  \"ts\": 1680000000,\n  \"actor\": {\"id\": \"u-123\", \"type\": \"user\"},\n  \"action\": \"grant_role\",\n  \"resource\": \"project:acme\",\n  \"details\": {\"role\": \"admin\"}\n}\n```\nProblems: customers say this is too technical and leaks internal IDs. also no explicit field for KMS key usage or byok events.

samir: +1 on adding a `customer_visible` shape and making `actor.id` obfuscated for exported examples. proposal: canonical name format `actor.action.resource` for humans, and keep machine_name for internal lookups.

irene: can we avoid multiple name fields? proposed fields: `event_name` (human readable), `event_id` (stable machine id), `visible_payload` (what we show customers), `internal_payload` (full). that way we can control redaction in exports.

maria.chen: I like that. also need to capture KMS usage for BYOK/key-rotation. sample new attributes: `kms.key_id`, `kms.operation` (encrypt/decrypt/rotate), and `consent_level` (customer_ack, implicit).

audit-bot: lint: event_name should use dot notation and be <= 4 segments. detected `grant_role` -> recommend `role.grant.project` :warning:

daniel.k: audit-bot suggestion is good but rename to `role.grant.project` or `project.role.grant`? Which reads better in splunk? @product-ops thoughts?

product-ops: prefer `actor.action.resource` ordering for UI grouping (so `user.role.grant`), product will map to label `User granted role on Project` for customer-facing docs.

samir: edge case — service principals and batch RBAC changes. We should include `actor.type` values: `user`, `service`, `api_key`, and add `batch=true` flag for bulk ops.

irene: vulnerability triage note: audit events that indicate privilege escalation should include `evidence` (list of related event_ids) so SOC can correlate, and `risk_score` for triage priority.

security-oncall: incident playbook needs event hooks for: `kms.rotate.failed`, `kms.rotate.succeeded`, `role.grant.privileged`. please ensure those exact machine IDs are emitted for alerting.

maria.chen: tentative schema snippet for customer export:\n```json\n{\n  \"event_name\": \"user.role.grant\",\n  \"event_id\": \"evt-21f3\",\n  \"timestamp\": 1680000000,\n  \"visible_payload\": {\"actor\":\"alice@example.com\",\"resource\":\"project:acme\",\"role\":\"admin\"},\n  \"meta\": {\"kms\":\"redacted\",\"customer_visible\":true}\n}\n```\nNote: `kms` redaction — we should never expose raw key IDs in customer-facing examples unless customer requests BYOK audit export.

daniel.k: migration plan: add new fields backwards-compatible, emit `legacy_event_name` until deprecated in 2 releases, provide a translation table in docs and SDKs.

samir: SDK change: add `export_mask` flag to decide whether `visible_payload` or `internal_payload` is returned via API. default to internal for internal APIs, visible for customer-facing endpoints.

product-ops: will prepare sample docs and handoff to support for FAQ about why some fields are redacted and how to request BYOK-level exports.

maria.chen: action items:\n- samir: PR for schema + audit-linter rules (ETA Wed)\n- daniel.k: migration doc + SDK mapping (ETA Fri)\n- product-ops: customer docs + FAQ (ETA Fri)\n- irene/security-oncall: list of high-risk event machine IDs for playbooks (ETA Tue)\n
irene: also add tests for redaction (unit + e2e) — I'll draft test cases.

audit-bot: reminder: subscribe to `#eng-security` for schema-change alerts. :bell:

maria.chen: thx everyone. we'll sync Thurs 9am if PRs land. :thumbsup:
